description: What hydrostatic head in millimeters means for a tent fly and floor, why seams matter, and which ratings suit your camping weather.
directAnswer: A tent's waterproof rating is the height of a water column, in millimeters, that its fabric resists before leaking. Look for 1,500 to 2,000 mm on the fly and 3,000 mm or more on the floor, with taped seams, since seams and setup decide whether you actually stay dry.
